newsitem.title: GUAM: Two more Korea air crash survivors die in hospital. [CORRECTED 7:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Two more Korea air crash survivors die in hospital. [CORRECTED 7:39 GMT]

text.p: The number of survivors from a Korean Air Lines jumbo jetliner crash dropped to 27 on Thursday when two more injured people died in hospital, a spokesman for the Guam government's media centre said.

"Two others died today," the spokesman told reporters in a briefing on the latest situation on search and recovery operations where the plane went down early on Wednesday morning with 254 (corrects from 264) people aboard.

U.S. military teams at the crash site in the jungles of Guam earlier on Thursday suspended efforts to retrieve the bodies of about 100 people still believed to be inside the KAL Boeing 747's severed fuselage.
"There may be about 100 more bodies in the fuselage, said U.S. Air Force Colonel Al Riggle, the senior officer coordinating the military search and recovery on Guam, a U.S. territory.
"But the military is waiting for the National Transportation Safety Board personnel to arrive on the scene, who then will take over from us."

Korean Air Lines (KAL) Flight 801 crashed into the jungles called Nimitz Hill, about three miles (five km) from the tropical Pacific island's international airport early on Wednesday just before it was due to land after a flight from Seoul.
